2) Shared function detection and scope/export behavior - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - DEFAULT_SCOPE: ```ts export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = [ "FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction", ]; ``` - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES for use by both rules. - `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)`: - Filters by node.type in scope. - Applies `exportPriority` = 'all' | 'exported' | 'non-exported' using `isExportedNode`. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - In create(): ```ts const scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE; const exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || "all"; const should = (node: any) => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority); return buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode: should, scope, exportPriority }); ``` - buildVisitors (src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts) creates visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, ArrowFunctionExpression. - ArrowFunctionExpression handler is gated by `options.shouldProcessNode(node)`, and since DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include 'ArrowFunctionExpression' and the schema enum does not permit it, arrow functions are effectively excluded from enforcement by default and not configurable via `scope`. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - create() returns visitors for: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (skips when `parent.type === "MethodDefinition"`), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Uses same `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES` (via shouldProcessNode), so both rules enforce on the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), with arrow functions excluded.
3) JSDoc/comment parsing and error location - @story/@story detection (require-story-annotation): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - `jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node)` uses `sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node)` and checks for "@story". - `commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node)` uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and scans for "@story". - `leadingCommentsHasStory(node)` inspects `node.leadingComments` for "@story". - `linesBeforeHasStory`, `parentChainHasStory`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` (from ./require-story-io) extend detection using source text and ancestors. - `hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node)` orchestrates all these heuristics under try/catch for robustness. - Error location: - `reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, target?)` resolves - `name` from id or key (with fallback ""). - `nameNode` from `node.id`, `node.key`, or node itself. - Calls `context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, ... })`. - `reportMethod` similarly uses the method key for `node` and includes both `name` and `functionName`. - @req detection (require-req-annotation): - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - Uses `sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node)`, `node.leadingComments`, and `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` via helpers `getJsdocComment`, `getLeadingComments`, `getCommentsBefore`, `combineComments`. - Delegates to `hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node)` in src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - Implements common detection strategy: - `linesBeforeHasReq`, `parentChainHasReq`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq` (using LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW) plus direct JSDoc/comment scanning. - All wrapped in try/catch to handle malformed/missing source info. - Error location and message: - `reportMissing(context, node, enableFix)` computes `name` via `getNodeName`, constructs `nameNode` from id/key/node, and reports with: ```ts context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingReq", data: { name, functionName: name }, ...(enableFix ? { fix: createMissingReqFix(node) } : {}), }); ```

"all"; const shouldCheck = (node: any): boolean => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority); ``` - All visitors call `runCheck(node)` which uses `shouldCheck`.
5) TypeScript-specific support - require-story-annotation visitors: - TSDeclareFunction: `buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor` => `helperReportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, node)`. - TSMethodSignature: `buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor` => `helperReportMissing` using resolved target. - require-req-annotation visitors: - `TSDeclareFunction(node: any) { runCheck(node); }` - `TSMethodSignature(node: any) { runCheck(node); }` - Shared TS RuleTester setup: - tests/utils/ts-language-options.ts exports `tsRuleTesterLanguageOptions` using `@typescript-eslint/parser`. - withTsLanguageOptions helper attaches these options to RuleTester cases.

traceability.notes: Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented. The plugin defines both `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` rules, sharing the same function-like detection scope (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) and common scope/exportPriority semantics. Arrow functions are excluded from enforcement by default. Both rules use ESLint’s SourceCode APIs to parse JSDoc and surrounding comments, report errors at appropriate function identifiers with clear, actionable messages, and support TypeScript constructs. Robust helpers handle malformed or missing JSDoc/comments with try/catch guards. Comprehensive RuleTester suites and dedicated helpers exercise JavaScript and TypeScript behavior, configuration options, autofix behavior (for @story and @req), and error reporting. Rule documentation exists for both rules with usage examples and configuration, and the full Jest test suite passes. Therefore all acceptance criteria for this story are satisfied.
